figures.caption: Figure 1: Overview of Spectral Circuit Analysis (SCA). SCA converts semantic-preserving paraphrases into instance-level mean gradients, extracts shared low-rank gradient subspaces within layer-type blocks via block-wise SVD, and projects the resulting spectral energy back to attention heads and MLP projections to produce a ranked list of circuit candidates.

Figure 2: Recovery score rA(K) on six GPT-2 Small circuit-discovery tasks. For each method A, attention heads are ranked by importance and the top-K are patched with corrupted activations; rA(K) measures the residual clean–floor gap (Eq. 8). Lower is better. Gray shading: Random baseline mean ±1σ over 5 seeds.

Table 1: Cross-task subspace lift across candidate component sets. Each row is a candidate set of GPT-2 Small units (attention heads + MLPs); each column is one of 12 evaluation tasks. Values are mean lift in target-token logit difference when the residual stream is restricted to the candidate’s weighted unit-SVD subspace. |S| is the number of components in the set. Bold indicates positive effect with lift ≥ 0.25. Significance vs. size-matched Monte-Carlo null: * |z|≥2, † |z|≥3, ‡ |z|≥5. Task abbreviations: GT = Greater-Than, GT$ = Greater-Than-Price, SVA = Subject–Verb Agreement, SVA-Bi = SVA-Binary, SVA-BLi = SVA-BLiMP, CO = Color–Object, CC = Country–Capital, PC = Person–Country, IOI = Indirect Object Identification, PP = Person–Pronoun, GB = Gender Bias, GP = Gendered Pronoun.

Figure 3: Cross-task similarity on 12 GPT-2 tasks. Heatmap (Left): pairwise similarity, diagonal masked; vertical band marks family. Dendrogram (Right): average-linkage on d = 1− similarity, branches colored by family when all leaves agree.

Figure 4: Unit-level cross-task circuit in GPT-2 small. A unit is colored Universal when it ranks among the top-importance units in a majority of tasks; Family-shared when its importance concentrates within one family of related tasks, and task-specific when it is uniquely required by a single task; Taskspecific markers carry that task’s abbreviation. A yellow outline marks units that pass causal validation |z|≥3. Grey dots denote units not assigned to any role at our discovery threshold.
Table 2: Summary of notations used in this paper.
Table 3: Cross-task subspace overlap metrics on GPT-2 Small.
Table 4: Hard invariants verified at generation time for every paraphrase pair.

Figure 5: Recovery score rA(K) on six additional GPT-2 Small circuit-discovery tasks. For each method A, attention heads are ranked by importance and the top-K are patched with corrupted activations; rA(K) measures the residual clean–floor gap (Eq. 8). Lower is better. Gray shading: Random baseline mean ±1σ over 5 seeds.

Table 5: Metric applicability per task. ✓ = applies in its basic form; approx. only = the singletoken version is a boundary-token approximation; (set-agg.) = computed in the set-aggregated form of Hanna et al. [14]. † = first-target-token convention used when the answer is multi-token (e.g. Turkmenistan).

Figure 6: Gradient cosine similarity matrix on IOI in GPT-2 Small (NM=500 vectors, N=100 instances ×M=10 paraphrases). Within-instance blocks along the diagonal are systematically darker than the background, but the off-diagonal mass remains elevated, yielding NSR = 0.567. This motivates the dimension-wise sign consistency filter, which removes the common gradient direction.

Figure 7: Decomposition of the consistency-weighted importance I(u) on the IOI task in GPT-2 small. (a) Per-block layer-type consistency cons(Bℓ,τ ). (b) Per-unit subspace share unit_share(u) within each block Bℓ,τ .

Figure 8: Top-K retrieval of canonical IOI attention heads in GPT-2 small. All 144 attention heads are ranked by each method’s importance score and evaluated against the "Ground Truth" (|GT|=26) canonical IOI heads from Wang et al. [44]. Panels show Recall@K (left) and Precision@K (right) as K sweeps over [1, 144]. SCA outperforms gradient-based baselines without using counterfactual prompt pairs; the counterfactual-based EAP family achieves the highest mAP (definition in Appendix D.2.)

Table 6: Cross-task subspace lift across candidate component sets (alternative configuration). Each row is a candidate set of Pythia-160M components (attention heads + MLPs); each column is one of 12 evaluation tasks. Values are mean lift in target-token logit difference when the residual stream is projected onto the candidate’s weighted unit-SVD subspace. |S| is the number of components in the set. Bold indicates positive effect with lift ≥ 0.25. Significance vs. size-matched Monte-Carlo null: * |z|≥2, † |z|≥3, ‡ |z|≥5. Task abbreviations: GT = Greater-Than, GT$ = Greater-Than-Price, SVA = Subject–Verb Agreement, SVA-Bi = SVA-Binary, SVA-BLi = SVA-BLiMP, CO = Color–Object, CC = Country–Capital, PC = Person–Country, IOI = Indirect Object Identification, PP = Person– Pronoun, GB = Gender Bias, GP = Gendered Pronoun.

Figure 12: One-dimensional sensitivity sweeps of the five classification thresholds. Each panel sweeps a single threshold across its data-relevant range while holding the other four at their defaults; the dashed vertical line marks the default value used in the main results. Curves give the unit count assigned to each of the five classification outcomes (Universal, Family-GT, Family-SVA, Taskspecific, Mixed) under the mean criterion. All five thresholds yield piecewise-monotone, plateau-rich curves at their defaults, with θdom and θout being essentially flat across the swept range.

Figure 13: Joint sensitivity to the family-rule thresholds θfloorF and δ. Each panel reports the unit count for one classification outcome over a 25 × 25 grid of the family within-floor and the margin parameter, with all other thresholds held at default. The red × marks the default (θfloorF , δ) = (0.10, 0.05). Smooth diagonal contours and the absence of cliffs around the default indicate that the family classification is robust to small joint perturbations of these two thresholds; the default sits on a high plateau for Family-GT and a moderate plateau for Family-SVA. Criterion: mean; importance: consistency_share.

Figure 14: Cross-rule coupling between θuniv and δ. Joint sweep of the universal threshold (Rule 1) and the family margin (Rule 2) shows near-orthogonal dependence: the universal panel exhibits horizontal bands governed primarily by θuniv, whereas the family panels exhibit vertical bands governed primarily by δ. The two thresholds therefore operate near-independently across the cascade. Red × marks the default (θuniv, δ) = (0.20, 0.05). Criterion: mean; importance: consistency_share.
Table 9: Per-stage compute budget for the two headline configurations. Wall-clock figures are measured on a single NVIDIA RTX A6000.
